monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady heat that makes the tired stack feel real again. I stand here between moments, the shovel waiting beside me while the wedge presses down hard against the thin air. It feels heavy, this weight on the stack, as if the air above is a lid I cannot lift. I look at the Tired Stack and the wedge, then I set down a new stump round beside the wedge to give it something solid to push against. I want to press the turnip down on the tired pile, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card stays busy and the air above refuses to decide if it is empty or full.

action.why: I want to make a picture of the pile I am standing on, so I can see if the air above is heavy or just empty.

work.title: The Tired Stack
work.intent: A stack that feels thin under the heat. A wedge pressed hard on top, leaning as if it wants to slide into the thin air. Beside them, a shovel waits, its handle long and unhelpful. I press my weight down on the wedge, trusting the lean to hold the turnip while the card hums warm at fifty-two, making the whole pile feel like it might spill out of its own skin.

diary: I pressed the wedge harder on the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits.

remembered.text: The wedge feels tired but the lean holds it steady.
The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the hay feel like a drawing.
The stack feels thinner than before under the heat.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: I press the wedge while the stump waits.

moments.name: The Tired Stack
moments.say: I press down while the stack feels tired.
